forecast_provider: Project model, not a NASA prediction
brief_favorable_conditions: Elevation > 15 m a.s.l., tropical maritime climate (25–31 °C), non-salinized halophytic grassland, no invasive rats.
why_these_variables: Heat and water supply for the herbaceous vegetation it fed and sheltered in. Sea-level rise and storm surge, the main documented threat, are not measured by NASA POWER and are not forecast here.

variables.label: Average monthly maximum temperature
variables.aggregation: Annual mean of each month's hottest-day temperature

variables.label: Annual rainfall
variables.aggregation: Sum of mm/day × days in month

t2m_max_mean.model_description: Average of (a) the mean of six simple forecasts (persistence, historical mean, recent mean, linear trend, Theil-Sen trend, autoregressive ridge) and (b) a global LightGBM model trained on every NASA series up to the cutoff year. Dry-season rainfall uses (a) only.
t2m_max_mean.interval_note: 80% band from pooled, standardized out-of-sample errors of the combined forecast (all distinct series, same horizon, only years up to the training cutoff).
t2m_max_mean.summary_text: Average monthly maximum temperature in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 29.2 °C (80% band for 2030: 28.6–30.0 °C; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 28.4 °C (+0.82 °C).

precip_annual.model_description: Average of (a) the mean of six simple forecasts (persistence, historical mean, recent mean, linear trend, Theil-Sen trend, autoregressive ridge) and (b) a global LightGBM model trained on every NASA series up to the cutoff year. Dry-season rainfall uses (a) only.
precip_annual.interval_note: 80% band from pooled, standardized out-of-sample errors of the combined forecast (all distinct series, same horizon, only years up to the training cutoff).
precip_annual.data_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.
precip_annual.summary_text: Annual rainfall in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 1,398 mm/year (80% band for 2030: 596.4–2,340 mm/year; coverage is not guaranteed), below the 1991–2020 average of 1,787 mm/year (-388.8 mm/year).
